PART O Introduction 1 GENERAL CONSIDERATIONS 7574 AND DEFINITIONS -- to contract values as agreed by the manufacturer and purchaser of the machine(s), This series of international Standards does not specify whether, or for which specific family of machines, the purposes mentioned above are relevant or whether the methods for determining and verifying stated noise emission values shouid be appiied. to ISO

In order to state the noise emission value for a machine or a batch of machines in an unambiguous manner, this four-part series of international Standards provides guidelines for determining the noise emission value to be stated ( e. g. as a Iabeiled value ) and These verification procedures. specifies methods are based on the premise of clearly defined acoustical measurement methods and describe the handling of the variability of the measurement results and, if relevant, of the noise emissions of the machines in a batch. The methods presented in this series of international Standards are compatible with the requirements specified in ISO 4871, i.e., -- the stated the limit value of specified emission ( e. g. Iabelled ) value Indicates below which the noise emission the individual machine and/or a large proportion of the noise values of the batch lies;

-- the stated vaiue is batch of machines.

For economic reasons, the stated vaiues for batches of series-produced machines may be verified by sampling procedures. This four-part series of International Standards does not deal with the consequences that ensue if the stated vaiue is not verified for a singie machine or for a batch ( iot ) of machines. This series of international Standards which comprise ISO 7574 requires that the iabeiled value be determined using the same measurement test code as that specified for verification. it, therefore, appiies to famiiies of machines or equipment for which speciai measurement test codes for the determination of noise emission quantities are prepared. If no special test code for a particular famiiy exists, the methods specified in iSO 3741, iSO 3742, iSO 3743, iSO 3744 and iSO 3745 may be appropriate.
NOTE -- This does not preclude the use of other International Standards, e. g. ISO 3746, which may form the basis of special measurement test codes,

-- the basic noise emission quantity used is the A-weighted sound power level. Although this series of International Standards is drafted mainly in terms of A-weighted emission sound power ievei as a noise quantity. It is equally applicable to other quantities. In this series of international Standard the is considered to inciude ali term "labei" means for providing information on the noise emission values to potentiai users \of the equipment; this inciudes iabeis, brochures, advertisements, commercial literature, etc. Requirements for this may be stipulated, for exampie, in a contract or in regulations. The methods described may be appiied not only to vaiues stated for iabeiiing purposes, but also to values stated for other purposes, for example: -- to the upper noise iimit set by an authority or specified in a technicai standard for a specific family of machines; `1

In each case the installation and operating conditions typicai for normai use shaii be cieariy specified or agreed,

IEC Publication 3 Definitions 3.1 sound power level, .Lw,in decibels : Ten times the logarithm to the base ten of the ratio of a given sound power to the reference sound power. The reference sound power is 1 pw. 3.2 A-weighted sound power level. LWA, in decibels : The sound power level of a noise source, determined according to an appropriate measurement test code with frequency weighting A ( see iEC 651 ) selected on the measuring instruments. 3.3 noise emission quantity; noise emission value : The basic noise emission quantity is the A-weighted sound power level, LWA, A single is called value of the noise emission a noise emission value, quantity 651, Souud /eve/ meters.

This part of ISO 7574 defines terms relating to methods for determining and verifying the stated ( e, g. Iabelled ) values of the noise emitted by machinery and equipment. International series of This four-part Standards applies both to machines which are produced in very small quantities as well as to machines which are produced by mass production methods. 2 References ISO 3534, symbols. 3.4 measured value : The noise emission value for an individual machine actually determined in accordance with an appropriate measurement test code.

3,5 family of machines : Machines or equipment of similar design or type, or intended to perform the same functions.
NOTES I A family may include different designs which meet the performance requirements, different production batches of a given design from one manufacturer, comparable products from different manufacturers in various countries designed to fulfil the same purpose or machines of different sizes but of similar design. 2 Examples of families of machines are a group of rotating electrical machines of a given range of power and speed, a group of concrete mixers with a certain range of volumetric capacities.

3.25 probability of acceptance, P, ( see ISO 3534): The probability that a batch of a given quality ( expressed by its proportion p of noise emission values exceeding the Iabelled value ) will be accepted by a given samp'ing plan.
NOTE -- ( 1 � Pa ) is called "probability of reject. ion". If ( 1 � Pa ) has the fixed value a ( see 3.27) , this is called the `producer's risk'. If Pa has the fixed value B ( see 3.28 ), this is called the "consumer's risk".

3.19 total standard deviation, w: The square root of the sum of the squares of the standard deviation of reproducibility ( see 317 ) and of production deviation of the standard (see 3.18): d 3.20 reference standard deviation, CM: A total standard deviation ( see 3.19 ) specified for the family of machines under consideration which is considered to be typical for batches from this family, NOTE -- The use of a fixed UM for each family
enables the application of a statistical method to deal with small sample sizes. If the actual total standard deviation ut is known to be different from o~~, the Iabeller estimates his risk of rejection on the basis of both standard deviations, at and UM. Typical values of uM range from 1s5 to 3"5 d@cepending on the precision of the measurement method used and on the complexity of the noise source. Extensive tests may be needed to establish @ for a family of machines.

3.26 operating characteristic curve, OC: A curve showing, for a given sampling plan, the probability of acceptance P, of a batch as a function of its proportion p of noise emission values exceeding the Iabelled value.
NOTE -- The operating characteristic determined by two specified points ( producer's risk point ) ( see 3.27 ) mer's risk point ( see 3.28 ) or by example the producer's risk point ) size rr. curve is fully for example, the and the consuone point ( for and the sample

3.21 single sampling ( see ISO 3534 ): A type of sampling which consists of taking only one sample from the batch. 3.22 double sampling ( see ISO 3534 ): A type of sampling which consists of taking possibly a second sample according to the information given by the first. 3.23 sequential sampling ( see ISO 3534): A type of sampling which consists of taking successive items, but without fixing their number in advance, the decision to accept or reject the lot being taken as soon as the results permit, according to rules laid down in advance. 3.24 inspection by variables ( see ISO 3534): A method which consists of measuring a quantitative characteristic for each item of a population or of a sample taken from this population. The quantitative characteristic is the noise emission quantity.
NOTES 1 The method used in this four-part series of ISO 7574 for assessing the acceptability of a batch using previous knowledge of its standard deviation is called the u-method. The s-method ( assessing the acceptability of a batch using the standard deviation based on measurements of all the items in a sample ) is not considered in this four-part series of 1s0 7574.

3.27 producer's risk point ( see ISO 3534 ): A point on the operating characteristic curve corresponding to a predetermined and usually low probability of rejection a. This probability of rejection is called the `producer's risk", The corresponding quality level is the propi-a of noise emission values of the portion batch exceeding the Iabelled value.

3.28 consumer's risk point ( see ISO 3534) : A point on the operating characteristic curve corresponding to a predetermined and usually low probability of acceptance ~, This probability of acceptance is then cal[ed the "consumer's risk". The corresponding batch quality is the proportion pR of noise emission values of the batch exceeding the Iabelled value and this is called the limiting quality. 3.29 level difference, AL: A value which, for a fixed producer's risk point, is used to take the consumer's viewpoints into consideration, and this is done principally by selecting an appropriate sample size, n. AL, when subtracting from the Iabelled value LC ( i. e, L'c = L, -- LL ), would give a low Iabelled value L'C with such a high proportion, pp, of noise emission values exceeding L'@ that acceptance would only be possible with a very low probability, (+( see 328 ),
